A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MEVA framework and applications. The complete text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across the extensive reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original Boston Housing experiments, Laplace and Burgers solver evaluations, and synthetic aggregation examples.

after.justification: v2 retains original PDE and synthetic results and reports revised Boston Housing results in Section 4.1.

M1.justification: The core error-estimation and variance-aggregation procedures remain, including variants relocated to Appendices D–F. The Boston kernel implementation changes from a sum of kernels on inputs and model predictions (v1 Equation 34) to a kernel on predictions alone (v2 Equation 13), altering that implementation's inputs.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Boston Housing regression, Laplace and Burgers equations, Gaussian PDE-solver aggregation, and the same two pathological examples. Moving examples into appendices introduces no new dataset or test scenario.

E2.justification: The Boston comparison removes support vector regression: it appears in v1 Figure 4 but not v2 Figure 2. The other individual-model comparators, mean aggregation, kernel aggregation, and two DNN aggregation approaches remain. PDE comparator membership is unchanged.

E3.justification: Boston evaluation reporting changes from MAE and MSE to MSE alone, and its reported kernel configuration changes from two Matérn length scales to one. The Laplace 500/100 training/test split and 100-by-100 evaluation grid remain unchanged. These reported revisions do not establish which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v1 Section 5.2.1 reports testing Fourier-coefficient aggregation and finding it inferior; v2 Section 4.2.1 retains the possible formulation but omits that comparative finding. The pathological examples, covariance-basis and bias-correction checks, and PDE case studies are retained, often in appendices.

E5.justification: v2 Section 4.1 newly states that Boston results are averaged over many splits. Neither version supplies split counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or error bars. This is additional reporting of repetition, not evidence of an explicit increase in runs.

E6.justification: Boston results and rankings change, and the MAE results disappear. Whereas v1 reports an advantage over equal-data individual models only in MAE, v2 reports MSE improvements of 7% over training-set Gradient Boosting and 2% over the best equal-data model. These are revised-setting results, not a controlled cross-version gain. Both PDE tables retain every value, including aggregate scores of -6.282 and -3.106.

T1.justification: v2 adds Theorem 1 and Appendix A: a decomposition of optimal MEA weights, a population-loss relationship, and perturbation arguments claiming different convergence rates for MEVA and MEEA. This substantial theoretical development is absent from v1. The earlier vector-valued GP material is retained in Appendices G–H.

C1.justification: v2 elevates a claimed rigorous faster-convergence guarantee to the abstract and principal contributions, extending v1's empirical and illustrative case for MEVA. It also explicitly claims the first aggregation of outputs across ML and classical PDE-solving methods and emphasizes structured scientific-computing applications.

C2.justification: Unlike v1 Section 4.1's statement equating unbiased MVA with MEA, v2 distinguishes MEA's lower population loss from MVA's claimed estimation stability. Section 3.2 and Appendix A.4 introduce interpretations involving scarce data, target-error correlation, and an equal-rate exception when t=0. The existing validation-data and no-guaranteed-improvement limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies Gauss–Newton optimization for the second pathological example and details GP-solver covariance calculations. Conversely, Appendix B omits v1's explicit 60-interior-point count and fixed-boundary/uniform-interior sampling details. The repository link remains available; these changes concern documentation rather than demonstrated implementation changes.

R1.justification: Related work shifts from a broad ensemble-learning overview to substantial discussion of model averaging and surrogate aggregation, adding works such as Hansen, Lee and Choi, Liu, and Liang. v2 positions MEVA against cross-validation weighting heuristics and distinguishes aggregation of fixed black-box models from jointly trained ensembles.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, contributions, related work, and discussion are substantially revised. The main exposition prioritizes the independent-error formulation and new theorem, while existing examples, general covariance treatment, bias correction, alternative loss, and GP derivations are reorganized into Appendices B–H.

P2.justification: v2 removes the aggregation flowchart, separates the paired pathological-example figure, replaces Boston's two-panel display with one MSE plot, and places the PDE tables side by side. Several unchanged figures move to appendices, alongside substantial changes to typography, spacing, and overall conference-paper layout.

improvement.justification: v2 improves comparison with close prior work and discloses averaging Boston results across splits, but its central new theoretical justification has a substantive inconsistency. Appendix A defines a quadratic loss minimized at alpha*=C^-1 gamma, implying L(alpha)-L(alpha*)=(alpha-alpha*)^T C(alpha-alpha*), with no first-order term. Equation 74 nevertheless asserts a generally nonzero first-order N^-1/2 term to support slower MEEA convergence. The clearer positioning and reporting, unchanged PDE evidence, and central proof problem leave the net quality direction uncertain.
